label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road network segments (crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends) on dirt ground

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground terrain tile set viewed straight down. It is a 176x192 field of speckled dirt and gravel with grey-teal cracked asphalt strips forming a crossroads, T-junctions, an L-bend, a dead-end square and an isolated patch. Road edges have a dark shadow line along their south sides, but it reads as a ground-level edge, not a raised front face. Nothing has a vertical south face of 3 or more rows, and there is no object volume, so it is a flat top-down terrain surface. For terrain kind this is the expected presentation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 8 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills: the dirt has speckle and grain in brown, red-brown and dark brown, and the asphalt has light crack dots and chips. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans blue-grey beside the asphalt and brown beside the dirt rather than being a black sticker line. The asphalt ramp is fairly shallow at about 4 steps (mid, dark, light chip, dark crack), and the dirt pattern repeats visibly. Even so, the 13 total colours and the information per tile are comparable to the paving reference, and the road segments do show crossroads and dead ends. A careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking thinner or flatter.
